observations: Read the entire pinned paragraph and its placement under section 6.5.1.4 on the full physical page 370, printed 285. It contains inline notation, not a displayed or numbered equation.
Relative roughness is visibly (k/D), with lower-case k, upper-case D and an ordinary slash. There is no exponent on k or D.

The first Reynolds threshold is greater than 10 with superscript 7: 10^7, not 10^6. The normal Reynolds range is 4,000 to 10 with superscript 6: 4,000 to 10^6. The comma in 4,000 is printed. No inequality sign is printed; greater than is prose.

The paragraph first states roughness depends on Reynolds number (hence velocity and diameter) and relative roughness (k/D). For Reynolds number greater than 10^7 the friction factor ‘f’ (and hence the C-value) is relatively independent of diameter and velocity. For normal ranges 4,000 to 10^6 it does depend on diameter, velocity and relative roughness. The applicability field faithfully retains both regimes and the qualifier relatively.

LaTeX and readable fields preserve k/D, both powers, the threshold direction and comma grouping; the LaTeX comma grouping 4{,}000 is rendering notation. The readable field includes normal; applicability supplies Reynolds-number context. Textual summaries need not reproduce typographic quotation marks around f.

The empty symbols list does not assert an absent definition. No k or D definitions are printed in this paragraph, and none are invented. The note correctly identifies Ep370-1 as a service locator without a printed equation number. The entire paragraph ends within the crop; no mathematical continuation is cut off.
